title: SQLite runs in WAL mode with a 5000 ms busy timeout and a pool of 4 connections
what: Apply ADR 0021 before any Click is written. Every pooled SQLite connection gets WAL journal mode and a busy timeout of 5000 ms, set through the sqlite-jdbc driver's connection properties in the Spring datasource configuration (not a PRAGMA in a migration). This way a new database, an existing Release 1 database and the test databases all behave the same. The Hikari pool grows from 1 to a fixed 4. There is still one data source, and the Link Store boundary is unchanged (ADR 0002). docs/onboarding.md explains that the data directory now holds links.db, links.db-wal and links.db-shm together, that backups must stop the app or use SQLite's online backup, and that the directory must be on a local file system. Spec 0003: Implementation Decisions (SQLite concurrency), Impact Analysis (Data flows). ADR 0021.
acceptance: application.properties sets spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=4 and passes journal_mode=WAL and busy_timeout=5000 (ms) as sqlite-jdbc connection properties on the single data source. No migration contains a PRAGMA

An integration test checks that the context's connections report journal mode `wal` and a busy timeout of 5000 ms. A TestApps instance started on a Release 1 database (created before this change, with Links in it) also comes up in WAL mode and still Redirects its existing Links
The whole existing ./mvnw verify suite passes unchanged with the new settings, and IntegrationTest's Flyway reset still works with WAL on
docs/onboarding.md documents the three database files, how to back them up safely, the local-disk-only requirement, and how to revert (PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE with no other connection open)
The plan 0001 traceability matrix gains a row for this ticket

title: Click Classifier: reduce Referer and User-Agent to Referrer Host, Agent Category and Device Class
what: Build the pure Click Classifier in plain JUnit 5, test-first, the same way the rules unit tests work. Raw Referer and User-Agent header values go in. Out come an optional referrerHost, an AgentCategory (BROWSER, BOT, OTHER) and a DeviceClass (DESKTOP, MOBILE). Referrer Host: a valid http/https URI with a host gives the host in lower case, without port, user info, path or query; anything else (missing, malformed, other schemes such as android-app:) gives none. Agent Category is checked in order: (1) bot if the user agent contains any of the maintained crawler/link-preview patterns, matched case-insensitively and kept in one place (bot, crawler, spider, slurp, facebookexternalhit, embedly, whatsapp, skypeuripreview, bingpreview); (2) browser if it starts with `Mozilla/`; (3) otherwise other, including a missing user agent and tools such as curl, wget and python-requests. Device Class: mobile if the user agent contains Mobi, Android, iPhone or iPad; otherwise desktop, including bots and missing user agents. Raw values are never stored or logged (ADR 0013). This ticket doesn't wire anything into the Redirect. Spec 0003: stories 8–12, Implementation Decisions (Click Classifier), Testing Decisions seam 2.
acceptance: ClickClassifier unit tests cover Referrer Host: upper-case host lowered; port and user info dropped; path and query dropped; missing Referer; malformed Referer; non-http(s) schemes (e.g. android-app:, ftp:) give no host
Real-world user-agent strings for Googlebot, Bingbot, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, WhatsApp and Discordbot are classified as bot. The pattern list has its own unit tests
Chrome and Firefox on desktop are browser/desktop. Safari on iPhone and Chrome on Android are browser/mobile
curl, wget, python-requests and an empty or missing user agent are other/desktop
A crawler user agent that starts with `Mozilla/` (e.g. Googlebot's) is still bot (bot before browser)
The classifier is pure (no Spring, no I/O, no logging of its inputs). Test names use the glossary terms

title: Record one Click for every successful Redirect (tracer bullet: Redirect → Click Recorder → Click Store → clicks table)
what: The end-to-end slice. Add the Click value (shortCode, clickedAt as a UTC Instant from an injected java.time.Clock, optional referrerHost, agentCategory, deviceClass). Add Flyway V2__create_clicks.sql: a clicks table with id integer primary key; short_code text not null; clicked_at text not null, ISO-8601 UTC in the same format as links.created_at; referrer_host text nullable; agent_category text not null, CHECKed to browser/bot/other; device_class text not null, CHECKed to desktop/mobile; an index on (short_code, clicked_at); no foreign key to links. Add the ClickStore interface (save a batch of Clicks in one transaction; list the Clicks for a Short Code, oldest first) and JdbcClickStore (JdbcClient, plain SQL, batch insert). It is the only code that touches clicks. Add the ClickRecorder interface (record(Click): returns immediately, never throws) and the queued Click Recorder: a bounded queue (offer, never put), one background writer thread that takes up to batch size Clicks, waits at most the flush interval for a batch to fill, and saves each batch with one Click Store call. It also offers flush() and stats() (recorded, dropped, pending). Settings: shortener.clicks.queue-capacity (CLICK_QUEUE_CAPACITY, 10000), shortener.clicks.batch-size (CLICK_BATCH_SIZE, 500), shortener.clicks.flush-interval (CLICK_FLUSH_INTERVAL, 1s), bound in ShortenerProperties. LinkController.followLink builds a Click through the Click Classifier after the Link Store returns a Long URL for a GET, hands it to the ClickRecorder, and returns the same 302 as before. 404s and HEAD requests record nothing. The test harness flushes the Click Recorder before the Flyway reset, so no Click leaks into the next test's database. It also exposes Click helpers that read through the Click Store, and supplies a fixed Clock. Plan 0001 principle 1 is amended to declare the Click Store as a seam until R2, and P8 moves to Release 2 with status in progress. Spec 0003: stories 1, 5–7, 13, 21, 23–26, Testing Decisions seams 1 and 3.
acceptance: A successful GET Redirect stores exactly one Click with the Short Code, the fixed clock's time, the expected Referrer Host, Agent Category and Device Class. This is observed through the Click Store's list operation after ClickRecorder.flush(), never by sleeping
A 404, a path that can't be a Short Code, a HEAD request, Link creation (POST /links and the web page form) and GET / store no Click
N Redirects of one Link store N Clicks, oldest first. Clicks for two Links stay separate
The full Referer URL and the raw User-Agent sent with the request appear nowhere in the stored Click
The V2 migration applies to an empty database (the per-test reset) and, through TestApps, to a Release 1 database that already contains Links, which keep Redirecting
The existing Redirect tests (MockMvc and RedirectOverHttpIT) pass unchanged: same 302, Location and Cache-Control: no-store
The three click settings bind from the environment variables with the stated defaults
No SQL touching clicks exists outside JdbcClickStore. No test asserts on SQL or reads the table directly
Plan 0001: principle 1 amended for the Click Store seam, P8 moved to Release 2 and marked in progress, matrix rows added for each criterion

title: Click loss is bounded, counted and logged: full queue, failed batches, batch size and stats
what: Make the queued Click Recorder's overload and failure behaviour explicit and proven with unit tests that use a stand-in Click Store (the in-app fault seam R14 allows), with no timing guesses. When the queue is full, record() drops the Click, increments the dropped count and returns immediately. A batch that fails to save counts all its Clicks as dropped and logs a warning with the count only; the writer carries on with no retry and the next batch is saved. Batches never exceed the batch size. Drop warnings are rate-limited to at most one line per flush interval and carry the number dropped since the last line, never a referrer, user agent, Short Code or Long URL (ADR 0013, ADR 0015). The writer logs its start and stop. stats() reports recorded, dropped and pending correctly. record() never throws: any unexpected failure inside it is caught and counted as dropped. Spec 0003: stories 3, 14–17, 19, 20, Testing Decisions seam 4.
acceptance: With a blocked stand-in store and a small capacity, Clicks beyond capacity are dropped and counted, and record() returns without waiting
With a stand-in store that fails one batch, every Click in that batch is counted as dropped, a single warning with the count is logged, and the next batch is saved and counted as recorded
With more queued Clicks than the batch size, no save call receives more than batch-size Clicks
stats() reports the expected recorded, dropped and pending numbers in each scenario above
Repeated drops within one flush interval produce at most one warning line, carrying the accumulated count. Captured log output contains no referrer, user agent, Short Code or Long URL
record() never throws, even if the queue or the clock misbehaves

title: Prove the Redirect never waits for or fails because of Click recording, including under SQLite write contention
what: Integration evidence for stories 2, 3 and 22, and the concurrency test ADR 0021 requires. (a) A stand-in ClickRecorder that blocks, and one that throws, swapped in through a @TestConfiguration the same way as the scripted ShortCodeGenerator: the Redirect still returns its 302 with Location and Cache-Control: no-store, promptly. If the Redirect handler needs a guard so that handing over a Click can never throw into the Redirect, add it here, test-first. (b) With WAL on, a stand-in Click Store holds a Click batch write transaction open: a Redirect lookup completes while that write lock is held, and Link creation succeeds once the writer releases the lock within the 5000 ms busy timeout, instead of failing with SQLITE_BUSY. Use the existing test context mechanisms (shared context or TestApps) without breaking plan 0001's isolation principle. Spec 0003: stories 2, 3, 22, Testing Decisions (Redirect never waits or fails; Concurrency). ADR 0021 Consequences (Tests).
acceptance: With a ClickRecorder stand-in that blocks indefinitely, GET /{short_code} returns 302 with the expected Location and Cache-Control: no-store within a short bound
With a ClickRecorder stand-in that throws a RuntimeException, GET /{short_code} still returns the same 302
While a stand-in Click Store holds an open write transaction, a Redirect of an existing Link completes with its 302 before the transaction is released
While the Click writer holds the write lock for less than the busy timeout, POST /links succeeds with 201 once the lock is released
Tests don't assert on SQL or table contents and don't sleep for fixed times to pass. Coordination uses latches or similar

title: Queued Clicks are saved on a normal shutdown, within the shutdown timeout
what: Run the queued Click Recorder as a Spring SmartLifecycle bean whose phase makes it stop after the web server stops taking requests. On stop it flushes until the queue is empty or the shutdown timeout passes. Clicks still queued then are counted as dropped and logged (count only), and the writer thread ends. Add shortener.clicks.shutdown-timeout (CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, default 10s) to ShortenerProperties. Spec 0003: story 18, Implementation Decisions (Queued Click Recorder, stop), Impact Analysis (Shutdown), Testing Decisions seam 3 (shutdown survival) and seam 4 (stop).
acceptance: Integration: with TestApps, an instance started with a long flush interval serves a Redirect, its context is closed normally, and a new instance on the same database file finds that Click through the Click Store

Unit: with a stand-in store, stop() saves everything queued when the store keeps up, and when the store is blocked beyond the shutdown timeout, stop() returns within about that timeout and counts the unsaved Clicks as dropped with one warning
The lifecycle phase makes the recorder stop after the web server's graceful shutdown, so Redirects served during shutdown are still recorded
CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT binds with a default of 10s
